title: Dropout as a Bayesian Approximation: Representing Model Uncertainty in Deep Learning
summary: Deep learning tools for regression and classification fail to capture model uncertainty, while Bayesian models provide a mathematically grounded but computationally expensive framework. This paper develops a theoretical framework casting dropout training in deep neural networks as approximate Bayesian inference in deep Gaussian processes, enabling the extraction of uncertainty estimates from existing dropout models via Monte Carlo (MC) dropout. The method achieves considerable improvement in predictive log-likelihood and RMSE compared to variational inference and probabilistic back-propagation baselines across multiple regression datasets, without sacrificing computational complexity or test accuracy.

requirements.stmt: Implement the theoretical framework casting dropout as approximate Bayesian inference in a deep Gaussian process, recovering the standard dropout objective L_dropout (eq. 1) from the GP objective L_GP-MC (eq. 4) via the KL divergence (eq. 3).
requirements.quote: Setting E(yn, by(xn, bωn)) = -log p(yn|xn, bωn)/τ we recover eq. (1) for an appropriate setting of the precision hyper-parameter τ and length-scale l.

requirements.stmt: Use MC dropout to estimate the predictive mean by averaging T stochastic forward passes through the network (eq. 6).
Estimate predictive variance as the sample variance of T stochastic forward passes plus the inverse model precision τ^{-1} (section 4).
Compute model precision τ from weight-decay λ and prior length-scale l using τ = sqrt(l^2 / (2Nλ)) (eq. 7).
Find optimal τ via Bayesian optimisation (e.g., Spearmint) over validation log-likelihood, with BO runs of 40 iterations and subsequent training with 10x more epochs than PBP's 40 epochs.
requirements.quote: The BO runs used 40 iterations following the original setup, but after finding the optimal parameter values we used 10x more iterations, as dropout takes longer to converge.

requirements.stmt: Use a network with 1 hidden layer containing 50 units and dropout probabilities 0.05 and 0.005.
requirements.quote: We used dropout with probabilities 0.05 and 0.005 since the network size is very small (with 50 units following (Hernández-Lobato & Adams, 2015))
